steps.body: A decimal is read by its last place: 0.62 is read “sixty-two hundredths,” because its digits end in the hundredths place.
steps.narration: A decimal is read by its last place: 0.62 is read “sixty-two hundredths,” because its digits end in the hundredths place.

widget.prompt: Shade the grid to show 0.62. Each full column is one tenth; each cell is one hundredth.

commonCounts.feedback: That shades only 2 single cells. The tenths digit of 0.62 is worth whole columns: 6 full columns first, then 2 more cells.
That count swaps the digits of 0.62. The first digit after the point counts full columns; the second counts single cells.

widget.successFeedback: Exactly 62 of the 100 cells — 6 full columns and 2 more cells: 62 hundredths, written 0.62.
widget.lowFeedback: The shaded amount is still below the target. Fill whole columns for the tenths digit first, then single cells for the hundredths.
widget.highFeedback: The shaded amount has gone past the target. Each full column is one tenth — check the tenths digit before adding single cells.

predict.prompt: You will shade 0.62 of the grid. Read aloud, what is this amount called?
predict.reveal: The digits of 0.62 end two places after the point — in the hundredths place — so the amount is named 62 hundredths.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g4d read decimal.
invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for g4d read decimal must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines g4d read decimal.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

explanationVariants: 0.62 is read "62 hundredths" — the digits end in the hundredths place.
The name counts the hundredths: 62 of them.

widget.prompt: How is the decimal 0.62 read as a number name?

options.label: 6 hundredths
options.feedback: That reads only the first digit after the point. The name uses the full count: both decimal digits of 0.62 together name 62 hundredths.

options.label: 62 ones
options.feedback: 62 ones would be the whole number 62. Digits after the decimal point count parts of a single whole, not whole units.

options.label: 62 hundredths
options.feedback: Correct — the last digit of 0.62 lands in the hundredths place, so the whole two-digit count 62 names hundredths.

options.label: 62 tenths
options.feedback: 62 tenths would be 6.2 — more than one whole. The two digits of 0.62 end in the hundredths place, so the count names hundredths.

hints: Where does the last digit land?
Two places after the point means hundredths.
